title: Accept intervention re-scores in squashed commits in the history check
summary: The history check's score validation (jobs.rs check → expected_score) recomputes a re-score from the squashed tree and wrongly rejects re-scores that `athena intervene --job` wrote legitimately. The fix makes squashes carrying interventions pass and keeps forged re-scores refused, with a regression test.

defaults_applied.how: A regression test for squash plus intervention re-score accompanies the fix; the whole suite and clippy stay clean.
One focused change to the re-score validation in athena-gate.
Behavior criteria name the cargo test commands the verifier can run.
Comments and any decision-log entry explain the squash case for an outside reader.

assumptions: The false failure comes from expected_score() in jobs.rs recomputing the closing score from the final squashed tree (all interventions, all records), whereas the recorded re-score was derived by rescore() from the earlier closing score at intervention time. I did not run a simulated squash, so the exact differing field is unconfirmed; the producer must reproduce it first.
The fix stays in the checker (athena-gate), keeping the forged-re-score refusal intact, rather than changing how scores are written.

acceptance_criteria.text: The root cause of the false 'does not follow from job X's records' for an intervention re-score in a squash is identified in code comments or the commit message, citing the differing field(s).

crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs no longer reports a re-score as not following from the records when the squash tree holds the closing score, the intervention and its re-score for the same job, as `athena intervene --job` writes them.
A new test builds a squash (chain or single job) containing a landed job plus an intervention and its re-score, and asserts check() returns no violations. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.

The existing test hand_written_scores_and_outcomes_are_refused still passes: a forged perfect re-score (all Brier values zeroed) with a real intervention is still refused with 'does not follow'. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle hand_written`.
cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check all pass.

out_of_scope: Exempting commits from the history check (D66/D67).
Changing how athena intervene writes scores.
departures: Higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference: the root cause is not yet reproduced, so the producer must first build a squash fixture with an intervention.
